original_test_intent: Verify every expected CPU0 through CPUN power-cap channel is correctly identified and its configured value, unit, status and thresholds are human-readable and match the approved CPU power policy and BMC sensor specification.
original_method: Enumerate all expected CPU power-cap resources and immutable raw/UI identities, collect complete cap value/unit/status/threshold and policy metadata with synchronized live package-power and thermal context, capture WebUI rows and compare each cap to the owner-approved range and semantics without writing it.
manual_activity: The owner defines socket/cap mapping, control-versus-sensor semantics, approved range and policy; an operator verifies the WebUI/raw representation and the owner adjudicates anomalies.
required_inputs: SUT/BMC/firmware and populated CPU socket inventory
CPU socket to SDR/Redfish/control/UI cap mapping
Cap unit/scale/permitted range/threshold semantics and active power policy
Read-only live package-power, utilization and temperature context
UI cache/rounding tolerance, protected access and evidence/redaction policy
safety_requirements: Keep the entire check read-only; never set caps, thresholds, governors, workload or thermal policy
Use protected authentication and complete non-truncated enumeration
Bind every cap value to its CPU socket and active policy
Preserve logs and stop/escalate on out-of-range caps, policy mismatch, thermal alarm, missing/duplicate mapping or health fault
Do not force a workload merely to reach the cap or retry after changing state
agent_execution_scope: Enumerate and verify the full CPU power-cap population and socket mappings
Collect complete cap/control metadata, immutable identities and timestamps plus live read-only context
Assist with synchronized WebUI capture and approved unit/rounding normalization
Report per-socket missing, extra, stale, out-of-policy or mismatch conditions for owner verdict
Perform no power-policy mutation or independent DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Supply authoritative cap-resource mapping, range, threshold semantics and policy
Resolve sensor-versus-control exposure and raw/UI/live-power discrepancies

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: ipmitool may expose a value, but a literal CPU0~N sensor name and head-limited fallback cannot establish all sockets, whether the value is a cap/control, its policy association, complete thresholds or UI correctness.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Securely enumerate complete sensor and power-control resources, select every owner-mapped CPU cap, collect full read-only metadata and live-power context, and correlate the WebUI representation to the approved policy.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CPU0~N_PWR_Cap scope, WebUI path, reading/threshold/spec comparison and 1/0-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH PACKAGE-GATED CPU POWER-CAP POLICY VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a per-socket matrix containing cap resource identity, configured watts/range/status/threshold/policy, live package-power context and UI display, with missing/extra/duplicate and policy-comparison results.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds cap-versus-live-power semantics and policy binding while replacing insecure/truncated reads and log clearing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A plausible watt number does not prove that it is the configured cap or covers all sockets. Every cap resource, policy field and raw/UI association must be checked.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some platforms expose caps as writable controls rather than threshold sensors. Read-only retrieval must be proven, and live package power need not equal a cap when the CPU is not constrained.

project_override_considerations: If CPU power caps exist only in a policy service or are shared across sockets, the owner must define the authoritative resource and expected population; the preceding package-power measurement remains a distinct case.
expected_evidence: Exact source row/variant/hash and SUT/BMC/firmware/CPU topology/policy revision
Per-socket cap/control resource to raw/UI identity matrix
Complete configured cap/unit/range/status/threshold/policy metadata and timestamp
Synchronized live package-power/utilization/thermal context plus WebUI comparison
Per-socket discrepancies, read-only/no-log-clear audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria coherently request power-cap readings/settings against specification. Sensor-versus-control exposure and policy semantics are owner inputs, not an internal source contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Mapping, approved power policy, complete read-only metadata and UI/context inputs gate execution while static review remains complete.

review_improvement: Separates configured power-cap policy from live power and requires complete per-socket read-only resource and UI correlation.
independent_technical_reasoning: A power cap is a configured ceiling, so equality with instantaneous package power is neither required nor generally expected. A raw watt-like value can be misidentified if sensor and control namespaces overlap. Correct validation must bind the resource to a socket and active policy, compare it with the allowed range, and use live power only as context. Because the resource may be writable, discovery and collection must be demonstrably read-only.
